title: Conservation of the Mediterranean fan mussel Pinna nobilis: adult growth in natural environment vs culture conditions
content:
ABSTRACT
This study investigates the growth rates of Pinna nobilis, an endangered bivalve species, under pre-mass mortality event conditions in the Embiez Archipelago, NW Mediterranean, France (43°04′N, 05°46′E). A total of 32 individuals were monitored over 12 months, with half maintained in their natural habitat and the other half reared under controlled laboratory conditions. The captive group was housed in continuous-flow mesocosm tanks with aeration and fed a supplemental diet of three microalgae species. Key environmental parameters (temperature, salinity, pH and photoperiod) remained unaltered to reflect natural conditions. Growth performance was comparable between the two groups. Individuals in captivity exhibited a maximum shell length increase of 3.1 cm, while those in the wild reached up to 2.0 cm. Average monthly growth rates were 0.10 ± 0.04 cm·month⁻¹ in captivity and 0.07 ± 0.05 cm·month⁻¹ in natural conditions. These findings suggest that P. nobilis can maintain similar growth rates in laboratory settings, indicating the feasibility of ex situ conservation approaches. This study provides a valuable foundation for developing rearing protocols aimed at supporting the conservation and potential restoration of P. nobilis populations.
